# The Bank Stock Rout: Facts vs Fiction | The Weekly Wrap

First listed: 2025-10-17 | Evaluation cutoff: 2026-11-10

[Back to library](../README.md)

## Source versions

- [YouTube: The Bank Stock Rout: Facts vs Fiction | The Weekly Wrap](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=sPTGq9wr_kE) - 2025-10-17
- [Substack: The Bank Stock Rout: Separating Facts From Fiction | The Weekly Wrap](https://realeismanplaybook.substack.com/p/the-bank-stock-rout-separating-facts-17d) - 2025-10-17

Earliest listed publication among matched versions, not proof of an unedited contemporaneous archive. Claim timestamps refer to the reviewed version.

## Summary

The October 17 wrap uses bank earnings supplements to distinguish isolated commercial-credit problems from system-wide distress. It explains bank valuation through tangible returns, argues for a merger cycle and reiterates the value of efficient scale competitors such as Progressive.

His process of comparing institutions and sizing losses is stronger than a headline-driven crisis call. Yet he overstates the universality of 2009 capital raising and turns a preference for bank takeovers into an overly exclusive reason to own regionals. The future normal-cycle view remains contingent.

### 003. Strong advisory and trading results suggest an M&A cycle benefiting Goldman, Morgan Stanley and boutiques.

**Unresolved** | Steve Eisman | investment thesis | major

[Source at 2:47-3:31](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=sPTGq9wr_kE&t=167s) | Stance: asserted | Horizon: not stated

Current fee strength and a future massive wave are separate claims; the latter lacks a measurable duration and volume hurdle.

<a id="youtube-sPTGq9wr_kE-c004"></a>
### 004. Current bank disclosures do not show broad consumer credit collapse, and individual losses should be judged relative to bank size.

**Mixed** | Steve Eisman | explanation | major

[Source at 3:31-4:29](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=sPTGq9wr_kE&t=211s) | Stance: asserted | Horizon: not stated

JPMorgan disclosures support substantial profitability and detailed credit monitoring, while household data later show uneven rather than uniform stress. This does not prove no problems anywhere outside the bank sample.

Assessment test: Compare standardized credit flows, loss absorption and borrower mix.

- [JPMorgan Q3 2025 financial supplement](https://www.jpmorganchase.com/content/dam/jpmc/jpmorgan-chase-and-co/investor-relations/documents/quarterly-earnings/2025/3rd-quarter/4d1864a5-0376-4269-8271-24f7f49662ba.pdf) (2025-10-14): Net income was $14.393 billion and ROTCE 20%. The supplement provides detailed business-level credit, nonaccrual, capital and profitability data, allowing isolated losses to be compared with the balance sheet.
- [Household Debt Increased Moderately; Delinquency Transition Rates Remain Flat](https://www.newyorkfed.org/newsevents/news/research/2026/20261110) (2026-11-10): Official indexed release inspected; direct open failed. Q3 stock delinquency rose to 5.0%, but serious card transitions improved to 6.87% from 7.05% a year earlier; auto transitions 3.02% versus 2.99%. This is uneven stress, not a general new credit collapse.

<a id="youtube-sPTGq9wr_kE-c005"></a>
### 005. Commercial credit deterioration differs markedly across large banks.

**Unresolved** | Steve Eisman | explanation | major

[Source at 4:34-5:14](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=sPTGq9wr_kE&t=274s) | Stance: asserted | Horizon: not stated

The comparison requires aligned definitions and complete supplements for every bank; the inspected JPMorgan file alone does not verify every quoted peer percentage.

Assessment test: Compare matching loan populations, nonaccrual policies and dates.


<a id="youtube-sPTGq9wr_kE-c006"></a>
### 006. Zions and Western Alliance issues appear isolated rather than evidence of immediate sector-wide failure.

**Unresolved** | Steve Eisman | investment thesis | major

[Source at 5:14-6:16](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=sPTGq9wr_kE&t=314s) | Stance: asserted | Horizon: not stated

The word appear is appropriate, but absence of newly disclosed problems elsewhere cannot establish absence of all shared exposures.

Assessment test: Trace borrower connections, collateral and subsequent losses across lenders.


<a id="youtube-sPTGq9wr_kE-c007"></a>
### 007. Bank earnings supplements provide detailed evidence that can test a credit narrative.

**Right** | Steve Eisman | analytical principle | major

[Source at 6:28-7:04](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=sPTGq9wr_kE&t=388s) | Stance: asserted | Horizon: not stated

The JPMorgan supplement supplies divisional results, nonaccruals, charge-offs and capital measures. Disclosure quality does not guarantee that every hidden exposure is known.

Assessment test: Reconcile releases, supplements and regulatory filings.

- [JPMorgan Q3 2025 financial supplement](https://www.jpmorganchase.com/content/dam/jpmc/jpmorgan-chase-and-co/investor-relations/documents/quarterly-earnings/2025/3rd-quarter/4d1864a5-0376-4269-8271-24f7f49662ba.pdf) (2025-10-14): Net income was $14.393 billion and ROTCE 20%. The supplement provides detailed business-level credit, nonaccrual, capital and profitability data, allowing isolated losses to be compared with the balance sheet.

<a id="youtube-sPTGq9wr_kE-c008"></a>
### 008. Current commercial problems are insufficient to signal an imminent recession; the next downturn should follow the normal economy-then-credit sequence.

**Not testable** | Steve Eisman | investment thesis | major

[Source at 7:06-8:48](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=sPTGq9wr_kE&t=426s) | Stance: asserted | Horizon: not stated

He gives no recession date and explicitly says he does not know when one will occur. Aggregate resilience does not rule out a shock through another channel.

Assessment test: Define the recession window and distinguish bank from nonbank transmission.


<a id="youtube-sPTGq9wr_kE-c009"></a>
### 009. The GFC differed because deteriorating underwriting and credit losses helped cause the recession.

**Right** | Steve Eisman | explanation | major

[Source at 7:51-8:24](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=sPTGq9wr_kE&t=471s) | Stance: asserted | Horizon: not stated

The FCIC documents mortgage underwriting failures, leverage and financial amplification before and during the recession. It was not simply a normal unemployment shock.

Assessment test: Trace underwriting, funding and loss chronology.

- [Financial Crisis Inquiry Report, findings and chapters 4, 6, 7, 13](https://fcic-static.law.stanford.edu/cdn_media/fcic-reports/fcic_final_report_full.pdf) (2011-01-27): Investigative evidence documents fragile leverage/funding, fee and ROE incentives, deteriorating underwriting, and securitization dependence. Pages 61-64 describe pay incentives; pages 89 and 125 describe the origination chain; page 281 reports Bear near 38:1 and balance-sheet window dressing. Findings are not proof of a single exclusive cause.

### 010. Sustainable ROTCE helps explain bank price-to-tangible-book valuation differences.

**Right** | Steve Eisman | analytical principle | major

The supplement provides detailed business-level credit, nonaccrual, capital and profitability data, allowing isolated losses to be compared with the balance sheet.

<a id="youtube-sPTGq9wr_kE-c015"></a>
### 015. The only reason to own regional banks is a takeover, while CEOs resisting sales harm shareholders.

**Not testable** | Steve Eisman | investment thesis | major

[Source at 14:11-14:53](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=sPTGq9wr_kE&t=851s) | Stance: asserted | Horizon: not stated

This is a strong investment preference, not a demonstrated universal truth. Standalone cash generation, capital returns and price can create other rationales.

Assessment test: Compare standalone valuation and sale proceeds under explicit scenarios.


<a id="youtube-sPTGq9wr_kE-c016"></a>
### 016. All banks were forced to raise dilutive capital in 2009, explaining their depressed long-run per-share paths.

**Mixed** | Steve Eisman | explanation | major

[Source at 14:56-15:38](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=sPTGq9wr_kE&t=896s) | Stance: asserted | Horizon: not stated

Dilution was important for some banks, but SCAP required additional equity at ten of nineteen assessed institutions, not all banks. Split adjustments and dividends also matter in return comparisons.

Assessment test: Separate institution-specific dilution, splits and total return.

- [SCAP capital requirements](https://www.federalreserve.gov/newsevents/testimony/bernanke20090603a.htm) (2009-06-03): Ten of nineteen assessed institutions were required to raise additional common equity. The requirement did not apply identically to every bank.

**Not testable** | Steve Eisman | analytical principle | major

## Framework and tools

- Use earnings to test the original thesis.
- Compare credit trends across banks and normalize losses by size.
- Link bank valuation to sustainable tangible returns.
- Distinguish a funding crisis from ordinary credit losses.

Tools and charts discussed, not a complete visual inspection:

- Nonaccrual loans
- Charge-offs and provisions
- ROTCE and price/tangible book
- Capital ratios
- M&A fees
- Insurance premium growth

## Source cautions

Steve Eisman presents; speaker attribution follows the full dialogue.
- Captions use ROCE where the intended bank measure is ROTCE.
- Fraud descriptions should be read as reported allegations or proceedings, not a finding against every associated borrower.
- He ends by admitting he cannot yet decide the competing AI-productivity accounts.
